cohort: 100 participants undergoing elective caesarean sections and abdominal hysterectomies.
finding: The short-term antibiotic regimen resulted in shorter hospital stays but increased infection rates and febrile morbidity, whereas the long-term regimen offered superior infection control at the expense of prolonged hospitalization.
mod_finding: For elective caesarean sections, the short-term antibiotic regimen was associated with higher wound infection rates (14% vs. 2%) and febrile morbidity (16% vs. 4%) compared to the long-term regimen, despite leading to shorter mean hospital stays (3.12 days vs. 5.24 days).
